A1.justification: Both PDFs describe MMSearch-Plus, its 311-task benchmark, Spatial-Temporal Extrapolation, and browsing-agent framework. All 18 pages of v1 and 38 pages of v3, including figures, tables, and appendices, support comparison despite substantial restructuring.

before.justification: v1 reports original model evaluations on MMSearch-Plus in Table 1, together with trajectory statistics and manually annotated failure analyses.

after.justification: v3 retains original evaluations and adds human performance, SoM-assisted browsing, text-only search, filtered-subset results, and tool-behavior analyses.

M1.justification: v1 supports cropping in principle but explicitly excludes it from the main experiments because models cannot reliably localize regions. v3 introduces an operational Set-of-Mark pathway: human-curated indexed boxes, raw and annotated image inputs, indexed zooming, and crop-seeded image retrieval (Section 2.5 and Appendix F). This substantially changes the agent's inputs and available procedure, without changing the underlying MLLMs.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same benchmark coverage: 311 image-based questions across eight primary categories, with identical primary-category counts. MMSearch+lite selects 239 existing tasks rather than introducing another domain or task. Its filtering belongs to evaluation protocol, while SoM changes the agent's assistance and tools.

E2.justification: v3 Table 1 adds an evaluated human/browser baseline and an o3 text-search-only comparator. GPT-5 also participates in the agentic Full Rollout + SoM comparison, whereas v1 evaluates it only without search and with image search. The underlying four-model roster remains unchanged; v1's human row contains only placeholders.

E3.justification: v3 adds the 239-task evaluation excluding questions answered without search by any tested model, a human protocol using Chrome for 10–20 minutes per task, text-only rollout, and marked-image SoM evaluation with a stated 20-tool-call limit. These are additional evaluation designs. The text-only budget is internally inconsistent: Section 3 states 20 rounds, while Section 5.1 states 10.

E4.justification: v3 adds SoM ablations, the internal-knowledge filtering analysis, inspection of 10 of 23 o3 easy-split failures, scene-text/OCR analyses, tool-transition and zoom-behavior diagnostics, and two detailed successful trajectories. The original trajectory plot survives as Figure 15. Conversely, v1's detailed o3 trajectory tables and its video-dependent failure case are removed.

E5.justification: v3 newly specifies seed 42 for selecting 30 supplementary task examples. This is a limited seed disclosure, not evidence of additional evaluation runs. Neither version reports repeated-run accuracy estimates, significance tests, or confidence intervals for the benchmark scores.

E6.justification: All 11 corresponding Table 1 rows are unchanged, including Full Rollout accuracies of 36.0/23.8/6.1 for o3/Gemini/Qwen. v3 adds SoM results of 37.6/27.7/7.1, GPT-5 + SoM at 35.4, humans at 22.8, o3 text-only search at 37.0, and the lite results in Table 4. These are additional conditions, not same-setting performance improvements. Detailed secondary-category counts and numerical trajectory summaries are removed.

T1.justification: Neither version develops formal theorems, proofs, or guarantees. Spatial-Temporal Extrapolation remains a conceptual curation procedure; the new conditional tool-transition frequencies are empirical analyses rather than new mathematical theory.

C1.justification: v3 makes SoM-assisted zoom-and-retrieve a headline contribution and claims consistent accuracy gains and improved multistep robustness. v1 emphasizes the benchmark and general browsing framework while acknowledging that full-scale cropping experiments were not conducted. The benchmark's central difficulty and Spatial-Temporal Extrapolation claims remain.

C2.justification: v3 attributes o3's easy-split failures primarily to skipping image search, distinguishes OCR-driven text search from visual retrieval, and explains different uses of zooming across models. It adds interpretations concerning internal-knowledge dependence and temporal benchmark drift. Appendix F also clarifies that human boxes bypass unreliable localization rather than demonstrate autonomous grounding. The original general limitations are retained within the Ethics Statement.

D1.justification: v3 provides SoM annotation and tool-interface details, the full system prompt, and executed tool traces (Appendices F, K, and L). It identifies Gemini as the webpage summarizer and reports an anonymized dataset-use archive and a 30-example supplement, replacing v1's project-page disclosure. The judge-consistency information is retained in Appendix G rather than newly introduced.

R1.justification: v3 adds discussion or citations for GQA, OK-VQA, InfoSeek, LiveVQA, SoM, and evaluated model reports. Table 2 now includes BrowseComp-VL and MM-BrowseComp, already discussed in v1. Most of the original literature review survives in Appendix D, and the central positioning around sustained reasoning from sparse visual cues remains.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, framework description, and results narrative are extensively rewritten. Contributions move earlier, the analysis section is reorganized, detailed related work and judge information move into appendices, and ethics and reproducibility statements are added. This constitutes substantial narrative restructuring beyond the insertion of new experiments.

P2.justification: v3 introduces a new opening paradigm diagram, relocates the original concert example to Figure 8, redesigns dataset statistics and accuracy tables, and adds performance comparisons, tool heatmaps, raster plots, zoom histograms, and annotated-image examples. Error cases are reformatted and reduced from four to three. The original trajectory figure moves to Appendix J, while several numerical appendix tables disappear.

improvement.justification: v1 emphasizes fine-grained visual reasoning but omits full-scale cropping evaluation. v3 substantially addresses that evidential gap through documented human-mark-assisted experiments, a text-only control, human comparison, and analyses of memory and tool-choice confounds. The prompt and tool specifications also materially improve reproducibility. Conflicting text-search budgets, Sports gains that do not match Table 4, and removal of detailed trajectory tables limit precision, but do not outweigh the stronger experimental support and transparency.
